questions.q: Where must a GitHub Actions workflow file live for GitHub to recognize it automatically?
options: It must be uploaded through a special GitHub Actions website
A separate settings page must register the file's path first
Anywhere in the repository, as long as it ends in .yml
.github/workflows/ at the root of the repository
questions.explain: GitHub scans .github/workflows/ automatically — committing a file there is the entire setup, no separate registration needed.

questions.q: Where do you find every workflow run for a repository, past and present?
options: A separate GitHub Actions dashboard on a different domain
The Issues tab
The Actions tab
The repository's Settings page
questions.explain: The Actions tab lists every run of every workflow file in the repository.

questions.q: What does a workflow run's summary page show?
options: Only the exact line of code that changed
The billing information for the entire GitHub account
What triggered it, how long it took, and whether each job succeeded
Nothing useful — you must read raw logs to know anything
questions.explain: The summary gives an at-a-glance view of the trigger, duration, and pass/fail status.

questions.q: According to this lesson, where do you actually go to debug a failing pipeline step?
options: Into the job's expanded step-by-step logs, to find the specific step that failed
The commit message of the triggering push
The repository's README file
You cannot debug a failure — you must re-run the whole workflow blindly
questions.explain: Expanded step logs show exactly which step failed and its output, rather than just an overall red X on the job.

questions.q: What triggers a workflow to run, based on the example in this lesson?
options: A human manually clicking a 'Run Now' button every time
The event specified under `on:`, such as a push
Nothing — workflows run continuously with no trigger
A scheduled email reminder
questions.explain: The `on:` key defines the triggering event — in the example, `on: [push]` runs the workflow on every push.
